entities.label: Institution
entities.summary: The Arif Agha Mosque, later known as the Imam Ahmad Ibn Hanbal Mosque, is a small Sunni mosque, located in the Rusafa area of the city of Baghdad, Iraq. The mosque was built during the Ottoman period, and it contains a small mausoleum which is purported to be the burial place of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, the founder of the Hanbali school of thought.
